page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i3g.4xlarge belongs to the Local SSDs family and operates on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz, supplying 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores with two threads per core. The hardware configuration features 64 GB of system RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The system includes 959 GB of bundled local SSD storage and a baseline network throughput of 5 Gbps. Discrete GPU acceleration is not present on this instance type.

Benchmark evaluations reveal reliable multi-threaded compute and solid data processing behavior alongside constrained single-thread performance. Single-core tests, such as stress-ng and gzip compression, place in the bottom 25% percentile. Conversely, multi-threaded metrics remain squarely in the middle tier, with stress-ng multi-core scoring 14,029.1 and Geekbench multi-core reaching 7,338.0. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth reaches 88.52 GB/sec and write bandwidth measures 46.7 GB/sec. Data processing capability is highlighted by PassMark database operations scoring 5,644.78 and Redis recording 13.73 million SET operations per second.

Given its integration of direct-attached local solid-state storage and dedicated compute resources, the instance delivers balanced throughput without the overhead of detached network storage. The primary hardware tradeoff is lower single-core execution speed and modest networking capacity compared to compute-optimized instances. Alibaba Cloud ecs.i3g.4xlarge is suitable for transactional databases, distributed NoSQL datastores, caching layers, and search indexing nodes where localized I/O density is essential.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i3g.4xlarge is a local storage instance configured with 16 dedicated vCPUs and 64 GB of memory, driven by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor at 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Featuring a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, the instance is equipped with 959 GB of bundled local SSD storage and 5 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth, with zero GPUs. Benchmark data demonstrates steady multi-core compute capability, with average results across Geekbench multi-core, PassMark, and Redis throughput at 13.73 million SET operations per second, contrasted with lower single-core execution performance in stress-ng and gzip workloads. These characteristics make the instance effective for operational databases, caching nodes, search backends, and low-latency storage workloads.
